description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NSF NHERI 2025: Terrain Effects on Turbulence and Structural Loads: A Wind Tunnel Study is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Nicholas Hrabik, University of Florida (ufl.edu). This project evaluates the effects of turbulence on wind pressures of buildings due to controlled terrain variations. The boundary layer wind tunnel was used to create a series of experiments and modify the statistical behavior of wind turbulence. The data from this project can be reused to explore other relationships connected to pressure coefficients. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 3 top-level files (PDF). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-y839-xs53. Keywords: Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel,  turbulence,  pressure coefficient,  terrain effects,  higher-order statistics, bluff body model. Published 2025-08-15. Facility named: Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel - University of Florida. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
